narrative.overview:
Each season's robot is launched the way a hardware company launches a product: the machine alone on an almost-black stage, lit from above, standing on a thin floor line. Then the page steps out into calm white and aluminium-grey reading pages that explain the robot, the people, the outreach and the partners. Light is the accent. There is no brand hue: colour comes only from the robots, the photos, the Mercury logo (kept as-is) and, on the partners page, the sponsorship package's four tier metals and the budget donut's validated palette (Andy asked for that page to be colourful, like the package).

Two grounds carry the site. The stage (home launch, every season head, the partners package sheet (head, tier chart and budget donut), and the closing "join or partner" bands on the home, team and partners pages) and the reading ground (white, with aluminium-grey bands and tiles). Sections are separated by a change of ground, never by hairlines. Since round 6 every page is a stack of defined boxes: each section is a rounded panel (28px corners, 20px on phones) on a mid-grey page ground (#D3D3DB) with 12px gaps (8px on phones), and the things inside a section sit on cards of their own. Content sits on flat, filled, rounded tiles (10/14/18px), buttons are pills, and nothing casts a shadow except a robot on its floor (the only other shadows are the small lift under the chosen outreach year and the halo around the part markers). One family, Archivo, does everything; robot names are set extra wide (125%).

The neutrals are our own: tinted from the logo's dark outline, not copied. The reference study of Apple, TechCrunch, Vogue, The New York Times Company and Prada specifically warned against reusing Apple's exact greys (#F5F5F7, #A1A1A6) and its 28px cards, which is why the values and radii here differ.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds: the near-black stage for launches and closing calls, white and aluminium grey for reading.
No brand hue; light, robots, photos, the logo carry the colour, plus the tier metals and the budget palette on the partners page.
Archivo only: normal width at 600 for headings, 125% width at 700 for robot names, tabular figures for every number.
Sections are panels on the page ground; items are cards inside them. Flat filled tiles with 10/14/18px corners, pill buttons, no section hairlines, no card shadows.
Selection shown as light brightening (the chosen robot steps into a spotlight), never as a sliding bar.
One authored load moment on the stage; everything else answers a click, tap or key. Nothing moves, fades, pins or changes while scrolling.

rules.name: The Light Is The Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no brand colour. Emphasis on the stage is brightness (a spotlight, full colour against dimmed grey); on light pages it is ink and weight. Don't introduce a hue for links, buttons or highlights.

rules.name: The Panel Rule
rules.body: Every section is a panel on the grey page ground: white panels for reading, aluminium panels for alternate sections, stage panels for launches, every page head, the partners package sheet and the closing calls. The things inside a panel sit on cards in the opposite fill (aluminium cards in white panels, white cards in aluminium panels, Stage Step cards on the stage), and whatever sits inside a card takes the card's opposite (`--card` / `--card-in`, set per panel in css/style.css "Panels and cards"). The footer is a panel too.

rules.name: The Metals Stay On The Partners Page Rule
rules.body: The tier metals and the budget palette colour the tier chart and the budget donut only. Text never wears them, except the tier names and amounts printed in ink on a metal fill; nowhere else on the site gets a brand colour from them.

rules.name: The Width Is The Voice Rule
rules.body: Only robot and game names go wide (125%, 700). Page titles, section heads and reading text stay at normal width.

rules.name: The Fixed-Place Figures Rule
rules.body: Every date, amount, spec and result uses tabular lining figures (`<time>` and `.num` get them automatically; spec, facts, figures, budget and season-fact values set them).

rules.name: The Flat Tile Rule
rules.body: Tiles, cards, menus and panels never cast shadows. A card sits inside a panel (that is the system), but a card never holds another card: inside a card, quotes, chips and photo frames take the opposite fill instead.

dos: Do change colours, sizes, radii and spacing in `:root` in `css/style.css`, never in a component rule.
Do use the stage only for a launch (home, season heads), the partners head with its tier and budget sheet, and the closing call to join or partner; put everything else on paper or aluminium.
Do put each section in a panel and each item (a write-up, a member, a program, a season, a post, a table) on a card in the opposite fill, with 18px corners and 16–24px padding.
Do make every button, toggle, tag and chip a pill; use `.btn` on light and `.btn--light` / `.btn--outline-light` on the stage.
Do set only robot and game names at 125% width and 700; keep everything else at normal width.
Do give every date, amount, spec and result tabular figures.
Do show a chosen state as light (brighter, full colour, filled dot) and write it to the URL when it is a view someone might share.
Do let new content simply be there: no entrance animation for anything below the first screen.
Do set `--w` to the image's pixel width on every `.photo`.
Do keep the sponsor strip in every footer, built from `SPONSORS` / `SUPPORTERS` in `js/main.js`.
Do add raster images only as the team's own photos or CAD renders, and record how any edited one was made (Assets and Provenance below).
donts: Don't add a brand hue, a purple or violet accent, or neon on black.
Don't copy Apple's exact neutrals (#F5F5F7, #A1A1A6) or its 28px cards; use the tokens here.
Don't separate sections with hairlines; change the ground instead. Lines belong inside data only.
Don't put shadows on tiles, buttons, menus or panels, or put a card inside a card.
Don't use the tier metals or the budget palette outside the partners page's tier chart and donut, and don't set text in them.
Don't add a second font family or system display faces.
Don't put small labels (eyebrows) above headings or number the seasons 01/02/03.
Don't add new load animations outside the stage, counters that tick up, or motion that ignores reduced motion.
Don't generate or invent images, results, sponsors or numbers; leave "TBD" instead.
Don't show a photo larger than its own pixels.
